subject: Stratotech — inference economics & competitive probe
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa@stratotech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next tests — inference economics / hyperscaler compare

Hi Lisa — great conversation this morning. Thanks for walking us through your latency and cost targets for the customer-facing summarization product. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations: 

1) Goals you reiterated:
- 95th pctl latency target: < 250ms on short requests (avg 128 tokens)
- Cost sensitivity: want to understand per-1M token economics across options and the impact of batching/caching
- Compliance: need VPC/private deployment later in Q4

2) What we committed to run as follow-ups (we'll provide artifacts attached):
- 1M-token synthetic run comparing Redwood Hosted (n1), Redwood Dedicated (reserved small pool), AWS Bedrock (p3/inf endpoints), and self-hosted Triton baseline. We'll capture per-token $ cost, 95th/50th latencies, and cost-per-conversation at various cache-hit rates.
- A cache-hit sensitivity sweep: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% prefix caching to show unit economics impact.
- Batching experiments: batch sizes 1/4/8/16 with tail-latency focused metrics.

3) Deliverables & timeline: 
- Today: sending benchmark instructions + matrix (attached).
- 48 hours: Redwood runs quick-hosted smoke tests and shares raw CSVs.
- 5 business days: consolidated comparison spreadsheet with annotated takeaways and recommended config for meeting your 95th pctl SLA.

4) Mutual action items:
- You: confirm the representative API prompts and the sample prompt distribution (short/medium/long) in the attached Excel.
- Us: validate the three model variants you called out (gpt-s-1, open-llm-v1, stratotech-custom) and map them to comparable open-topologies.

If that looks right, we'll start the runs today and loop in engineering (cc'ed) for any infra clarifications. Thanks again — excited to prove we can deliver better unit economics at-scale.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
---
Attachments: stratotech-matrix-requests.xlsx (spreadsheet, 43KB); 1M-token-benchmark-instructions.md (text, 6KB)

From: Lisa Chang <lisa@stratotech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@stratotech.com
Date: 2028-09-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next tests — inference economics / hyperscaler compare

Thanks Stephanie — this is exactly what we need. A few clarifications: 

- For the representative prompts, include a small percentage (~10%) of long-context requests (>=1024 tokens) to surface any degradation.
- We also run internal running-cost numbers that include data egress on hyperscalers; please call out egress assumptions per-platform.
- On models: we cannot share our custom model binary, but we can provide a behavior slice (10k requests) to replay against a compatible open topology.

Procurement is copied on the timeline; if the Redwood Dedicated numbers look compelling we'll move to a reserved capacity conversation. Can you also add a simple one-page TCO summary that uses per-1M token math and shows sensitivity to cache hit rate?

Appreciate it — Lisa
Lisa Chang
Sr. Product Manager — ML Platforms, Stratotech
lisa@stratotech.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: ops note — test plan and quick cost assumptions

Internal note so we have a clear methodology before runs: 

- Workload: 1,000,000 tokens synthetic mix (70% short <=128, 20% medium 129-512, 10% long >=1024) to match Lisa's ask.
- Platforms & mapping: 
  * Redwood Hosted: r-hosted-gpt-s-1 (fp16), batching auto, default cache TTL
  * Redwood Dedicated: reserved small (4x A100 equiv) with aggressive KV cache enabled + int8 quant where supported
  * AWS Bedrock: bedrock-infer-sim (p3-style) — include vendor-provided pricing & egress assumptions
  * Self-host Triton baseline: single-cluster optimized, includes network overhead typical of on-prem (no egress)

- Cost assumptions (ballpark for initial sim, will refine):
  * Redwood Hosted: $7.20 per 1M tokens (baseline)
  * Redwood Dedicated (reserved amortized): $4.70 per 1M tokens at 50% utilization
  * Bedrock-like hyperscaler: $9.30 per 1M tokens + variable egress
  * Self-hosted Triton: $3.80 per 1M tokens but with ops overhead and no SLA

- Cache sensitivity approach: compute effective per-1M token cost = raw per-1M * (1 - cache_hit_rate) + cached-cost-floor (engineering estimate $0.20 per 1M when cache hit). We'll sweep hits at 0/25/50/75%.

Action: I'll run the smoke-hosted tests today and drop CSVs in the Drive link. Marissa/Karthik — please help validate kernel selection and the quantization config for the Dedicated run.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa@stratotech.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-15T15:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next tests — inference economics / hyperscaler compare

Lisa — quick update from engineering and a small ask before we start the bigger dedicated runs: 

1) We completed the hosted smoke run and attached the short CSV with per-request latencies and token counts (uploaded to the Drive link). Initial headline: Redwood Hosted median latency 62ms, 95th pctl 210ms for short requests; cost matches Ben's ballpark.

2) Ask: please upload the 10k behavior slice you mentioned (prompt+expected response length) to the shared Drive folder. That lets us replay the slice across the self-hosted and Bedrock simulations so numbers are apples-to-apples. 

3) Next tests (planned):
- Dedicated run with int8 quant + KV cache enabled (target: 95th < 220ms, demo config)
- Bedrock pricing simulation including egress; we'll include both list price and committed-discount scenarios

I'll schedule a short sync next Tue to review the consolidated TCO chart and run through the cache-sensitivity visualization. If you prefer earlier, happy to jump on a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
